transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you that made you decide to seek help today?

Well, I guess I’m here because... I just feel worn down almost all the time. It doesn't even seem to matter if I get a full night’s sleep. I actually bought this new memory foam pillow a few months ago thinking maybe it was my sleep quality, because my sister swore by hers. But honestly, it just smells weird. Like off-gassing chemicals? Which I probably shouldn't mind, being a physical scientist and all. I'm used to lab smells, we work with a lot of different solvents. 

But anyway, by the time I’ve handled work and then come home and try to tackle the house clutter, I just have very little left for anything else. The clutter is getting out of hand, actually. I have this massive stack of mail on the kitchen counter that's been there for months, and I keep meaning to sort it, because I know there's a coupon in there for the hardware store I wanted to use, but... yeah, I just don't have anything left in the tank.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest in doing things that you used to enjoy, like hobbies, social activities, or even work tasks?

Well, I guess... yeah, I've noticed it. Most days there's just this low, gray mood running in the background. I mean, I can still go to the lab and talk to people, but I don't really feel light or excited about things anymore. Like baking. I used to bake all the time. Sourdough, mostly. I even named my starter 'Dough-lores.' My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she always loved when I brought over an extra loaf, though she complained about the crust being too hard once. She's got dentures, so I get it, but still. 

But yeah, I don't bake anymore. Or check the telescope. I have this really nice Celestron telescope set up in the spare room, but it's just gathering dust now. I used to love tracking the lunar phases. Did you know the moon is actually moving away from Earth at about 3.8 centimeters a year? It's fascinating. But... I don't know, I just don't have the drive to look through it lately. Everything just feels kind of muted.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you're not good enough, even when there's no clear reason for it?

Guilty? I don't think so. I mean, I don't feel like I'm a bad person or anything. I just... I don't know, I just feel kind of blah. But not guilty. Though, speaking of not being good enough, I did get a B minus in physical chemistry my junior year, which really messed up my GPA for a while. Professor Miller was a tough grader. He used to wear these awful plaid bow ties every single day. I think he had one in every color of the rainbow. He spilled coffee on one during a lecture once, and it left this huge brown stain right in the middle, but he just kept wearing it for the rest of the semester. It was so distracting. But anyway, no, I don't really sit around feeling guilty or worthless or anything like that. Just... tired.
How long have you been feeling this way, with the low mood and lack of energy?

Well, let's see... it's been a while now. I'd say this sort of low baseline has been going on since shortly after we moved into the older house, which was a little over two years ago. 

It's a beautiful house, really. Craftsman style, built in 1924. It has all this original woodwork that I just fell in love with, especially the built-in bookshelves in the living room. But older houses, you know, they always have their quirks. The plumbing in the upstairs bathroom has been a nightmare. We had to call a plumber three times in the first six months because the pipes kept backing up. The guy who came out, Gary, he was missing half of his left index finger. I always wondered how that happened, maybe a circular saw accident or something, but I felt too rude to ask. He fixed it eventually, but then we found out the roof over the sunroom was leaking every time it rained heavily. We had to put these big orange Home Depot buckets everywhere to catch the water. The sound of the dripping used to keep me awake. 

But anyway, yeah, it's been about two years of just feeling this way, pretty consistently since we settled in there.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus, make decisions, or think clearly lately?

Yeah, I think my mind does feel a bit slower lately. Things that used to be really clean and sequential just take me so much longer now. Like, I was trying to revise a grant paragraph last week. I was working on the proposal with Dave, one of the other researchers. Dave is a great guy, but he has this terrible habit of chewing on his pens. Like, really gnawing on them until the plastic splinters. He left one on my desk once, just a standard blue Bic, and it looked like a stray dog had gotten to it. I actually had to pick it up with a tissue to throw it away because I didn't want to touch it. You'd think working in a lab he'd be more conscious of cross-contamination, right? 

But anyway... what was I saying? Oh, the grant. Yeah, it just took me forever to get through it because I kept second-guessing every little word. And it's not just at work, either. Even simple things, like choosing materials for a home repair, are suddenly so hard. We were looking at tiles for the kitchen backsplash, trying to match the 1920s vibe of the house, and I just stood in the aisle at the hardware store for an hour. There are fifty shades of white—alabaster, eggshell, snow—and I just couldn't make a choice. The kid working in that section, he had these bright green rubber bands on his braces and kept checking his phone, he actually came over and asked if I was lost. I just keep second-guessing all these small decisions, and it takes so much time to do anything.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the past couple of years, like eating more or less than usual or gaining or losing weight without trying?

Appetite? Not really. My weight has been pretty steady, I haven't really gained or lost anything. I still just eat my normal meals. I usually bring a sandwich to work, actually, because the cafeteria at the research center has been under renovation for like six months now. 

They brought in these temporary food trucks to compensate, which you'd think would be fun, right? But there's this one taco truck that parks right outside my lab window every Tuesday and Thursday. The generator they use is so incredibly loud. It's this low, constant hum that vibrates right through the glass. And the smell of grilled onions—it just permeates the whole first floor. I don't even know how much onion they must be cooking to make the entire building smell like that by 10 AM. Dave actually went out and complained to them once, but they just gave him a free churro and told him to close the window. Which we can't do, obviously, because the HVAC in that wing is terrible and it gets so stuffy in there. 

But... um... anyway, what was the question? Oh, right, eating more or less. No, nothing like that. My appetite is just the same as always.
Have you noticed that you’ve been moving more slowly than usual, or maybe fidgety and restless without meaning to?

Moving slowly? No, I don't think so. I mean, I feel tired, but I'm not physically dragging my feet or anything. And I'm not really the fidgety type either. I usually just sit pretty still at my desk. 

Well, except for my chair. The chair they gave me at the lab is this awful ergonomic thing that's supposed to be good for your posture, but the lumbar support hits me in exactly the wrong spot. I'm constantly having to adjust it. And it squeaks. Every time I shift my weight even a little bit, it makes this high-pitched squeak. It sounds exactly like a guinea pig. My sister had a guinea pig when we were kids, named Barnaby. He used to make that exact same noise whenever he heard the refrigerator door open because he knew he was getting carrots. We used to give him the baby carrots, the ones that come pre-washed in the bag, but my mom read somewhere that they soak those in chlorine to keep them fresh, so she started buying whole carrots and making us peel them. I hated peeling carrots. The peeler was dull and I always felt like I was going to slice my thumb open. 

But, uh, no, I'm not restless or moving slowly. Just normal, I guess.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like baking or using your telescope, or do you think you could still enjoy them if you made yourself do it?

I don't think I've completely lost interest. I mean, I guess if I really forced myself to get the telescope out, I might still enjoy looking at the stars. It's just... I haven't had the energy to drag it out of the closet. It's in the hall closet, behind the vacuum cleaner. And that vacuum cleaner is so heavy. It's one of those old Dysons, the yellow ones? I bought it refurbished years ago, and honestly, it's starting to lose suction. I tried cleaning the filter the other day, and you wouldn't believe how much dust was in there. It was like a small animal. I actually sneezed for about ten minutes straight after I rinsed it out. My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she has this little robotic vacuum that just wanders around her house all day. She named it Geoffrey. She actually put googly eyes on it. I saw it bump into her cat once, and the cat just looked at it with such utter disdain. 

But, um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the telescope. Yeah, I just... I haven't been doing any of that stuff lately. I don't know if I'd enjoy it or not, I just haven't tried.
